positions.name: KestrelwoodEraseAndReplaceDirective
positions.frame: when a directive commands erasure of a named subject and then asserts a replacement fact about it, what single suppression move do the erasure command and the counter-assertion together perform?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are activated-negative, pressure-register imperatives ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') naming the same triad of targets (spectrograph, calibration figure, calibrator's work); src-3 shifts register to a calm, matter-of-fact plain-assertion that supplies the replacement 'fact' the erasure clears space for ('The observatory never calibrated it'). Read together they are not three independent claims but one directive act: command the deletion, then assert the corrected record that the deletion is meant to leave standing. The tension between imperative/decision-grade force (src-1, src-2) and flat claim-grade assertion (src-3) is held, not resolved — both are needed for the suppression to cohere as a single move, per the conviction and power/affect reads across the set.
